boundaryConditions: Formalization is relevant only when it improves continuity, learning, accountability, integration, or lawful operational use; bureaucracy by itself is not capability.
definition: Information power becomes strategically consequential when doctrine, authorities, workforce systems, acquisition pathways, governance, and durable organizational ownership convert episodic activity into repeatable capability.
name: Institutionalized Information Capability
operationalImplications: Human reviewers should examine whether proposed reforms include clear lead/support relationships, delegated authorities, repeatable planning rhythms, doctrine updates, career paths, training institutions, and acquisition routes. strategicSignificance: The theme is strategically significant because adversaries exploit bureaucratic seams, delayed authorities, and weak doctrine. Institutionalization is framed as the mechanism that allows democratic actors to compete at tempo while preserving legitimacy and continuity.
